summary: This note is a list of NFL franchise post-season streaks, focusing on consecutive playoff appearances and consecutive championships. The New England Patriots hold the longest active playoff streak at nine appearances, tied for the longest of all time, and won two Super Bowls during it. The Dallas Cowboys (1975-1983) and Indianapolis Colts (2002-2010) also had nine straight playoff appearances, and the Green Bay Packers hold the longest consecutive NFL title streak with three crowns, achieved in the 1920s and again in the 1960s.
one_line: Lists NFL franchises with the longest consecutive playoff-appearance and consecutive-championship streaks, led by the Patriots, Cowboys, Colts and Packers.
key_facts: The New England Patriots hold the longest active consecutive playoff streak with 9 appearances, starting with the 2009 -- 10 NFL playoffs.
The New England Patriots' nine-appearance playoff streak is tied for the longest of all time.
The New England Patriots won two Super Bowls during their current playoff streak.
The Dallas Cowboys had nine consecutive playoff appearances from 1975 to 1983, tying the record.
The Dallas Cowboys won one NFL championship during their 1975-1983 playoff streak.
The Indianapolis Colts tied the record with nine straight playoff appearances from 2002 to 2010.
The Indianapolis Colts won one championship during their 2002-2010 playoff streak.
The Green Bay Packers hold the longest consecutive NFL title streak, with three consecutive championships.
The Green Bay Packers won their three-consecutive-title streak once in the 1920s, before playoff games existed.
The Green Bay Packers won their three-consecutive-title streak again in the 1960s, winning seven playoff games during that three-year span.
